title: Compiled argument evaluation
statement: Let $Z$ describe a word-RAM layout with limits, and let a light state $σ$ be represented in a frame at stack position $q$ by memory $m$, with the frame within the stack bounds. Let $es$ be a list of expressions and $k$ a starting temporary index. Suppose every expression in $es$ has width at most $Z.F$ and is safe in $σ$ under the limits, and $k+|es|\le Z.F+1$. Then evaluating the compiled argument code yields, for each $i<|es|$, the $W$-bit encoding of the $i$th argument value in temporary cell $k+i$; throughout, memory is unchanged outside the temporary cells indexed from $k$ through $Z.F$.
